subject: Service Elevation for Renewal — proposed premium SLA & capacity plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jenkins <cjenkins@stellarsys.com>; Stellar Systems Procurement <procurement@stellarsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Service Elevation for Renewal — proposed premium SLA & capacity plan

Hi Claire / Stellar procurement,

Thanks again for the productive renewal check-in last week. As promised, attached is a short proposal that (1) formalizes the premium SLA your team asked about, (2) outlines the latency SLOs we can commit to at your increased commit level, and (3) proposes a support tier uplift with dedicated escalation paths. Key points up front: 

- Term: 12 months starting upon signature; option to extend to 24 months with additional discount (details in addendum).
- Premium SLA: 99.9% regional uptime, latency P95 target of 180ms for inference on the standard model family, plus pre-agreed fallbacks to a compatible lower-cost model during regional saturation.
- Capacity: baseline reserved capacity of 250 concurrent sessions (burst to 450) with auto-burst credits for Q1 onboarding spikes.
- Support: Dedicated TAM + 24/7 priority incident queue; up to 4 hours response for Sev 1 incidents, business hours for low/medium.

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_Stellar.pdf (draft addendum with redlineable clauses), usage_report_Q4_2027.csv (recent usage to justify commit).

Request: can you confirm procurement timeline and any internal reviewers we should loop in (legal, security)? If the terms look reasonable, I can circulate a redline-friendly DocuSign and schedule a 30-min alignment call with TAM + your ops lead.

Next steps I propose:
- Claire: confirm procurement window and any must-have legal changes by March 7
- If agreed, sign addendum via DocuSign by March 21 to lock new pricing/commit for April 1 start

Thanks — happy to hop on a call to walk through the SLO language.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182
From: Claire Jenkins <cjenkins@stellarsys.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Feb 2028 11:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Service Elevation for Renewal — proposed premium SLA & capacity plan

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear summary and the addendum. A few questions from my side and procurement: 

1) Can you clarify the metric you use for P95 latency? Is that measured at the platform edge per region or at the model runtime? Our ops team needs the exact signal for alerting.
2) The burst credits sound useful — are those one-time credits or a rolling monthly allowance?
3) We have an internal requirement to see SOC 2 evidence tied to any new SLA. Can you attach the SOC 2 report or provide the audit reference?

Procurement timeline: we need legal + security reviews before we can sign. Realistically, if the redlines are minor, we can get to signature by March 28. If there are material legal terms, it may slip to mid-April. Our procurement contact is procurement@stellarsys.com — looped above. Please also provide a customer-facing runbook for incident handoffs to share with our on-call team.

Claire Jenkins
Head of Platform Ops, Stellar Systems
claire.jenkins@stellarsys.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Marissa, Ben — forwarding Claire's reply (below). Procurement is asking for: clear metric definition for P95 (edge vs runtime), clarification on burst credit mechanics, SOC 2 evidence, and a runbook for handoffs. They are targeting signature by Mar 28 if redlines are minor.

Ask: can we accommodate a one-time onboarding burst credit package (e.g., 500k token credits) plus a monthly rolling buffer (say 50k tokens) without changing committed $ too much? Also want to know legal's appetite for the fallback-to-compatible-model clause (we have that to preserve availability when a model variant is unavailable).

I'm prepping a short runbook to send but need pricing guidance and an approval for the DocuSign envelope.

Rafael / Ben — I talked to Legal and Product Ops. Short answers: 

- P95 latency definition: measured at the platform edge (per-region ingestion point) for completed inference responses; we include guidance on in-flight retries and excluded maintenance windows in the addendum language. I can drop an exact measurement paragraph into the addendum to remove ambiguity.
- Burst credits: we can structure this as a one-time onboarding credit (500k token credits applied in month 1) plus a rolling monthly buffer of 50k tokens for months 2–3. After month 3, normal contract terms apply. That should cover their ramp without lowering baseline commit.
- SOC 2: attach link to the SOC 2 report in the DocuSign envelope; legal prefers reference to the audit artifact rather than attaching the full report in email.

Pricing concession: approve a one-time one-month credit equal to 8% of projected monthly committed spend (applied as token credits) and keep the committed AR at list. We'll mark this as a non-recurring concession tied to immediate signature. Ben — can you update the pricing worksheet and produce a final numbers page for the DocuSign?

I will prepare a short incident handoff runbook and add the P95 paragraph into SLA_Addendum_Stellar.pdf. Once Ben confirms the pricing sheet and Rafael confirms procurement window, we can send the DocuSign envelope.

Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Claire / procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal approvals below: 

Summary of agreed updates (attached redline + pricing sheet):
- P95 latency: measured at platform edge per region (definition paragraph included in addendum).
- Burst credits: 500k token onboarding credit (applied month 1) + 50k token rolling buffer for months 2–3.
- SOC 2: reference to audit artifact included in DocuSign; we will provide a secure link to our SOC 2 report as part of the signing package.
- Pricing concession: one-time credit (non-recurring) equal to ~8% of projected first-month committed spend, contingent on signature by March 21.
- Support: Dedicated TAM and 24/7 priority queue; Sev1 target response time 4 hours, escalation matrix included in runbook.

Next steps:
1) I have uploaded the final addendum and pricing worksheet to DocuSign and created envelope S-2028-0421 for electronic signature: https://docusign.com/remote/embedded?document=S-2028-0421
2) Please confirm who will sign from Stellar (name & role).
3) We will provide SOC 2 access and the incident runbook as secure links in the envelope.

If everything looks good, signing by March 21 locks the onboarding credits and the pricing concession. If procurement needs more time, let us know and we can agree a mid-April fallback plan (terms will remain similar but the one-time credits will be reduced).

Thanks — happy to schedule a short call to walk legal/security through the addendum text.

Best,
